data.question: If selected, what will I do?
data.answer: The GovLab Student Council will convene twice a month after school for one hour online.  There will be no expectation of work in between sessions.

data.question: If selected, what will I do?
data.answer: The ReinventED Student Council will convene twice a month after school for one hour online.  There will be no expectation of work in between sessions.

data.question: How many people will you select?
data.answer: Up to 15. We will convene in two Councils, one ages 14-17 and another ages 18-21.

data.question: Who is eligible?
data.answer: Students attending school within the United States in or out of schools ages 14-21 (as of January 1, 2021). International students who attend school within the United States are eligible.

data.question: How do I apply?
data.answer: To apply, students must complete a short application, record a brief video and sign the commitment to participate actively in the Council, if selected. Applications are due by December 10 at midnight.

data.question: What is the selection process?
data.answer: We will select up to 15 students to join ReinventED Student Council. We are looking to select a diverse range of students who demonstrate an interest in the topic and are willing to commit to participate actively.

data.question: When will you decide?
data.answer: We will notify you by December 15, 2020.

data.question: Why be a part of ReinventED Student Council?
data.answer:
1. Impact: Have the opportunity to inform the policy debate on assessment and education.
  2. Payment: We will compensate you for your participation with a $100 gift card.
  3. Learn Facilitation and Leadership: Students will work in pairs to take turns leading the sessions and work with us to learn how to develop an agenda and moderate.
  4. Improve Public Speaking: Students will get training in how to create a persuasive presentation and have the opportunity to present publicly to leading decision makers.
  5. Mentoring: Students will get additional one-on-one coaching and mentoring from university faculty and students. 
  6. Recognition: Be able to promote your experience on college and job applications.
  7. Friendship: Meet other engaged students.
